then: From his chair it is the same green book.

repeat: The scabbard is engraved with a battle honor. I would tell you which, but the engraving and the Colonel disagree.
Not a nick on it. Either it's the finest blade in the territory, or it's never met anything.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. It has never left this wall and it has never been sharpened.
repeat: Nothing. Steel at rest, and resting comfortably.
A faint ring when the door closes, and then it remembers itself.

overrides.PICK_UP: Never taken down, never sharpened. I'll honor both traditions.

LOOK_AT.say: A wide, shallow drawer in the sideboard, the kind printers keep plates in.
repeat: It does not quite close. A corner of card shows at the gap, the good heavy kind photographers use.

then: Fine joinery, for something nobody is meant to look in.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Whatever is in there is packed too tight to shift.
repeat: The runners squeak a little when the sideboard takes my weight. It has been opened recently.

repeat: The spines are all one thickness, year after year. Business in Consolation, it appears, never rises and never falls. It merely continues.
He has offered to let me read them, and I believe he would. That is how I know there is nothing in them.
then: Twelve years of accounts, bound handsomely enough to be believed.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. A shelf of figures that all agree with each other.
repeat: The shelf creaks under them. They are heavier than the business they describe.
Nothing. The particular quiet of a book that has never been audited.

LOOK_AT.say: Every claim in the district, pinned. Two of them have red pins. One is Claim One.
repeat: Green pins for the Company, a great many. The two red pins are alone together near the middle.
My pin has been pushed all the way in. The others merely rest. I don't know why that bothers me as much as it does.
Pins ticking against the cork in the draft. A small, busy, acquisitive sound.
Nothing. The map is entirely up to date and has nothing further to report.

LOOK_AT.say: Colonel Fanshawe, painted at approximately twice life size and one-third his actual age.
repeat: The uniform has more braid than a regiment would issue and fewer stains than a war would allow.
The painter has given him a battle in the background. It is not clear which battle. I suspect the painter was told several.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Which is the first honest thing about it.
repeat: Canvas, stretched very taut, like the story.
Nothing. In oils he is the strong, silent type, which is the only thing the painter added.

overrides.TALK_TO: The painted one listens exactly as well and commits to less. I prefer him slightly.

LOOK_AT.say: Eleven chairs, in a room that receives visitors one at a time.
repeat: Each one is turned slightly toward his desk, the way flowers turn toward a window.
Eleven chairs. I counted twice, and on the second count I had the strong impression I had been offered one.

LISTEN_TO.say: Leather, settling. They're extremely comfortable, and I don't wish to sit in one.
repeat: A cushion slowly breathing out. Somebody sat in it recently and was relieved of something.
Nothing. Good furniture in this town is very patient.

overrides.PUSH: They're heavier than they look. Everything in this office is heavier than it looks.

LOOK_AT.say: A tall window over Main Street, curtained in velvet the color of good port.
repeat: The glass is new, thick, and very slightly green. The town looks prosperous through it. That may be what the glass is for.
From here you can see the Assay Office door and the Registrar's, and how long the line is at each.
then: He can see the whole town from here, and the town can see him being generous.

LISTEN_TO.say: Main Street, with the edges taken off.
repeat: A wagon passing. Through this glass it sounds as if it is paying a call.
Nothing gets in that he has not let in. The street knocks politely and is not answered.
then: Even the noise is muffled into good manners in this room.

LOOK_AT.say: A safe the size of a small cabin, painted with roses and a landscape, as though money could be made to feel at home.
repeat: The landscape has a river in it, running gold, toward the handle.
He has never opened it in front of me. He has opened everything else.

LISTEN_TO.say: Nothing. Iron this thick has heard nothing since it was cast.
repeat: Nothing. It doesn't tick, which is the first thing I listen for in a lock.
A dull note when the floor takes my weight. Heavy things have very little to say, and say it low.

overrides.OPEN: Locked, and painted with roses. He keeps his money where it can be admired.

exits.name: THE DOOR

LOOK_AT.say: From this side it is a door like any other. From the lobby it is the most important door in the territory. He has arranged both.
repeat: The hinges are oiled so that it closes without a sound. Visitors find themselves inside before they have decided to come in.
There is no lock on this side. There has never been any need. Nobody leaves this office in a hurry.

LISTEN_TO.say: The lobby, faintly, and the clock out there being eleven minutes wrong.
repeat: Nothing. A door this well hung keeps every secret in the room and lets in only the draft.
Voices in the lobby, waiting. Everyone waits out there. Nobody waits in here.

LOOK_AT.say: An iron cabinet painted with a landscape, roses and gilt. It is a vault door dressed for dinner.
repeat: The landscape on it is a valley with a river and not one claim stake in it. The only untouched country in the territory, and he keeps it on a safe.
It has stood in this office every time I've been in it. I took it for furniture. I think that was the idea.

LISTEN_TO.say: The iron ticking faintly as the room cools. Something that size is never entirely quiet.
repeat: A cold draft at the edge of it. There's a room behind it, colder than this one.
Nothing from inside. Money is very quiet when it has been stacked properly.
